chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is manumitted for himself, whether he may place himself wherever he wishes and appoint as his patron whomever he loves.

He said: 'If he is manumitted for himself (for God), he is the slave of the one who manumitted him. And if he is manumitted and made a Sa'ibah, then he may place himself wherever he wishes and appoint whomever he wishes as his patron.'

key_terms.أَبَانٍ: Aban ibn Tahir al-Laythi, a prominent narrator
key_terms.سَائِبَةً: Sa'ibah (a type of manumission where the slave is free to choose their patron)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a slave manumitted for themselves and a Sa'ibah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between a slave manumitted specifically for the master's benefit, who remains the master's mawla, and one manumitted as a 'Sa'ibah' (free gift), who gains autonomy to choose their own patron. This ruling highlights the flexibility in manumission contracts within Shia jurisprudence, allowing for different legal outcomes based on the intent of the emancipation. The hadith underscores the principle that the nature of the gift determines the subsequent social and legal bonds of freedom.
